cse-2009-cs-6.approach: Rewrite AB + C in product-of-sums form, (A+C)(B+C), which maps directly onto a two-level NOR–NOR circuit; then show 2 gates are not enough.

steps.title: POS form
steps.body: By distributivity, $AB + C = (A + C)(B + C)$.

steps.title: Three NOR gates
steps.body:
$G_1 = \overline{A+C}$, $G_2 = \overline{B+C}$, $G_3 = \overline{G_1 + G_2}$.

$G_3 = \overline{\overline{A+C} + \overline{B+C}} = (A+C)(B+C) = AB + C$ (De Morgan). So **3** gates suffice.

steps.title: Two gates are not enough
steps.body: The function depends on all of $A,B,C$, so with 2 gates the output gate must take the other gate $G = \overline{x+y}$ and one variable $z$ (the only other wirings use at most 2 variables). Output $= \overline{\overline{x+y} + z} = (x+y)\,\bar z$, which is 0 whenever $z = 1$. But $AB + C$ can be 1 with $z = 1$ whichever variable $z$ is: $z=C$: take $C=1$; $z=A$ or $B$: take $A=B=1, C=0$. So 2 gates cannot work and the minimum is **3**.

answer.keyNote: The stored key is D (5), but $\overline{\overline{A+C}+\overline{B+C}} = (A+C)(B+C) = AB+C$ uses only 3 two-input NOR gates, and 2 gates provably cannot realise the function, so the minimum is 3 (option B). Flagged for review.

optionAnalysis.reason: Two NOR gates give at most $(x+y)\bar z$ — never $AB + C$.
Correct — NOR–NOR realisation of $(A+C)(B+C)$ needs exactly 3 gates.
4 gates work but are not the minimum.
5 is the count from the naive conversion (AND and OR each built from NORs), not the minimum.

cse-2009-cs-8.approach: Interrupts are sampled at instruction boundaries so that the interrupted program can resume from a clean, precisely defined state.

cse-2009-cs-9.approach: Belady's anomaly (more frames → more faults) can only happen for policies that are not stack algorithms; FIFO is the classic non-stack policy.

steps.title: Stack property
steps.body: Optimal and LRU are **stack algorithms**: the set of pages in memory with $k$ frames is always a subset of that with $k+1$ frames, so faults never increase with more frames.

steps.title: FIFO
steps.body: FIFO is not a stack algorithm. Reference string $1,2,3,4,1,2,5,1,2,3,4,5$ gives **9** faults with 3 frames and **10** with 4 frames.

optionAnalysis.reason: Correct — FIFO shows Belady's anomaly (9 faults with 3 frames vs 10 with 4 on the classic string).
Optimal is a stack algorithm — no anomaly.
LRU is a stack algorithm — no anomaly.
MRU ranks pages by recency independently of the frame count, so it is a stack algorithm — no anomaly.

cse-2009-cs-12.approach: Every derivation wraps a single middle symbol (a or b) in matching pairs, so strings are palindromes of odd length — and every odd palindrome can be built this way.
